sentences.text: For a UCB with a floating-rate loan, the rules say the bank may, at its option, provide a choice to switch to a fixed rate at the time of reset, rather than must offer it.
The bank’s own policy also says it may, at its option, offer the borrower a choice to switch to a fixed rate at the time of reset as per its Board-approved policy.
The older RBI circular on reset of floating interest rates is no longer in force on the as-of date.
I did not find an in-force rule requiring a mandatory fixed-rate switch offer at reset; the in-force UCB rule is discretionary and conditional.
